p:cNvPr.descr: A cross-section of the cell plasma membrane. The cross-section has the membrane tilted slightly toward the viewer so that the spatial relationships of surface proteins can be observed. The membrane has light yellow hydrophobic tails in the center, flanked at top and bottom by blue hydrophilic heads, shown as tiny blue circles. They are labeled “hydrophilic polar heads” below. The top of the membrane is labeled “outside” and the bottom is labeled “inside.” On the far left end of the membrane section is a glycolipid, which is a chain of small cyan blue hexagons. Among the hydrophobic tails are sterols, which are small orange cylinders embedded in the membrane. They can be seen on the top as well. To the right of the glycolipid is a large gray integral protein (single transmembrane helix) (labeled below), spanning the membrane. Its top and bottom ends are folded gray chains, and the center, which spans the hydrophobic tail layer, is a compressed zigzag. Bonded to the top of the integral protein is a larger chain of cyan hexagons, labeled “oligosaccharide chains of glycoproteins.” 3 other glycolipids are sprinkled on the surface of the membrane. Scattered across the membrane as well are pale purple globular proteins, which are anchored to the membrane by cyan blue chains. They are labeled “GPI-anchored protein” on the right. On the inside portion of the membrane, to the right and at the bottom, there is a larger paler purple protein, not embedded in the membrane but just below it. It is labeled “peripheral protein.” To the immediate right of this is a green protein, which is a large green sphere with a short tail linked to the membrane. It is labeled “peripheral protein covalently linked to lipid.” Scattered throughout the membrane as well are pale blue unlabeled proteins.
